transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (Sentinel CTO), Lina Torres (Sentinel VP Ops), Rajiv Patel (Sentinel Eng Manager)

Summary/Notes (auto): quick renewal/expansion check, talk through geocluster, private VPC needs, and contract amendment logistics.

[00:00] Jordan Li: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Marcus Hale: Marcus here, hi all.
[00:06] Lina Torres: Lina — hi.
[00:07] Rajiv Patel: Rajiv — on the call.
[00:09] Priya Nambiar: Priya from Redwood, hi.
[00:11] Jordan Li: Great. Agenda — stretch the commitment to 18 months to get better unit pricing, plan EU geocluster activation, and run a benchmark to validate latency and throughput. Sound ok?
[00:21] Marcus Hale: Yep that's the core. We want to avoid surprises on latency in EU, also data residency and KMS integration are big for compliance.
[00:28] Lina Torres: Budget window is tight; if we can lock terms by end of April procurement can cut a PO first week of May.
[00:33] Jordan Li: Understandable. Priya can you walk through the EU geocluster options and the typical provisioning timeline?
[00:38] Priya Nambiar: Sure — we have two paths: 1) Hosted EU region with dedicated capacity pool (fastest, 2–3 days for staging), or 2) Private geocluster in your VPC (longer, depends on networking + KMS, typically 2–4 weeks). For Sentinel's compliance ask, we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS/HSM. That gives the strongest audit trail.
[01:05] Rajiv Patel: Quick clarifying q: for private geocluster, will Redwood manage the control plane or do we need to host it?
[01:12] Priya Nambiar: We run a lightweight control plane but in a customer-dedicated VPC. You retain network control; we deploy inference nodes into a subnet you allocate. It does require some CIDR prep and peering/VPN setup.
[01:25] Marcus Hale: And KMS — we have an HSM provisioned, we'd like to integrate so keys never leave our environment. Is that supported?
[01:31] Priya Nambiar: Yes, we support customer KMS via direct HSM or cloud KMS integrations. There are extra steps for attestation and cert exchange but it's standard for our Private customers.
[01:41] Jordan Li: Great. Cost side — if we move from 12 to 18 months, we can give two uplift tiers: conservative (10% off current list) and aggressive (16% off) depending on commit amount and ability to pay upfront. I'll put that into a spreadsheet and share.
[01:58] Lina Torres: Can you model both with and without burst capacity? We need to see the delta if we need extra burst forpeak shopping events.
[02:06] Jordan Li: Absolutely. We'll show reserved baseline vs baseline+burst pricing.
[02:10] Marcus Hale: On performance targets — we need sub-60ms median for our token-limited prompts in EU, and p95 under 200ms during normal load; spikes may tolerate more./ Not sure if that's realistic with quantized models.
[02:24] Priya Nambiar: We should validate with a benchmark. For the EU geocluster we'll run a 5-day test: synthetic traffic and a replay of your production traces (anonymized). That will exercise batching and KV cache. If you provide the traces we'll do a replay.
[02:39] Rajiv Patel: We can scrub logs and send a 48-hour sample. There may be PII so we'll sanitize.
[02:44] Marcus Hale: We'll coordinate with security on that.
[02:46] Jordan Li: Good. Next, SLA & audit — you mentioned audit logs and retention. What retention window do you need?
[02:52] Lina Torres: For now 90 days is minimum; ideally a year for high-risk flows. We also need proof of SOC 2 and ISO or equivalent materials for our security team.
[03:02] Priya Nambiar: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary. Audit logs are configurable per tenant; 90 days default with optional extended retention as add-on. I'll attach the security whitepaper.
[03:13] Marcus Hale: Any lock-in concerns if we choose private? Eg can we switch back to hosted easily?
[03:19] Jordan Li: There's an operational delta — moving from private back to hosted is supported but may need data transfer and model pinning reconciles. We typically build a fallback policy in the rollouts.
[03:28] Rajiv Patel: Ok. On network design — are there specific ports, protocols we need to expose?
[03:33] Priya Nambiar: We provide a networking checklist. Primarily outbound to our control plane over TLS, and internal RPC for the nodes. We'll send the exact firewall and peering steps.
[03:44] Jordan Li: Pricing nuance — if you commit to 18 months and allow limited upfront payment (50%), we can lock the aggressive tier. If procurement requires monthly billing we can still do a middle ground.
[03:57] Lina Torres: Procurement prefers PO for the whole term but cash flow might force monthly invoicing with net-30. We'll check.
[04:05] Marcus Hale: On competitors — we ran a quick eval of ScaleServe last quarter. Their latency was good but they lacked the private KMS path; that was a blocker.
[04:15] Jordan Li: Noted.
[04:17] Priya Nambiar: For the benchmark, we'll instrument token-level traces and token cost breakdowns so you can see per-request economics. That usually helps stakeholders choose commit tier.
[04:28] Rajiv Patel: Good — cost per request is what the finance folks will want to see.
[04:32] Jordan Li: I'll include per-token cost at current quantization profile and one with more aggressive int8-like quantization assumptions.
[04:39] Marcus Hale: Any risks to model fidelity if we push quantization? We rely on extraction tasks so small shifts matter.
[04:46] Priya Nambiar: We'll run regen tests against your eval set during the benchmark and produce a simple quality delta report (rouge/bertscore-ish). It's not perfect but it flags regressions.
[04:58] Lina Torres: Great. Logistics — provisioning timeline if we sign the amendment end of next week?
[05:03] Priya Nambiar: For Hosted EU dedicated pool: we can stage in 3–5 business days. For Private geocluster with your VPC + KMS: plan 2–4 weeks depending on network approvals.
[05:13] Jordan Li: So worst case we get EU nodes up mid-May if we start now.
[05:17] Marcus Hale: That aligns with our Q2 product launch.
[05:20] Jordan Li: Any other red flags from security or legal?
[05:23] Marcus Hale: Legal wants to keep termination flex for model regressions — like if quality drops 10% on our evals. Is there a mechanism?
[05:31] Priya Nambiar: We can add a quality guardrail clause tied to predefined evals and rollback/fallback policies. We usually define mitigation steps before termination.
[05:40] Rajiv Patel: For the benchmark data send, do you need schema?
[05:43] Priya Nambiar: We'll send a template for traces and scrub instructions.
[05:47] Jordan Li: Action items recap: Jordan will send revised pricing and commitment tiers; Priya will schedule the EU benchmark week and share network checklist; Marcus to share compliance docs; Lina to confirm procurement window; Rajiv to send traces.
[05:58] Marcus Hale: We'll also loop in our security lead on the next call.
[06:02] Jordan Li: Perfect. Any final Qs?
[06:05] Lina Torres: One ask — can you include a sample contract amendment for quick review?
[06:09] Jordan Li: Yes I'll attach a draft amendment and highlight the key clauses for KMS, retention, and rollback.
[06:15] Marcus Hale: Thanks, that's helpful.
[06:16] Jordan Li: Ok we'll aim to have the pricing spreadsheet and draft amendment by Tuesday 2027-04-20, benchmark scheduled for week of 26th, and follow-up call on 2027-04-28 to finalize.
[06:27] Priya Nambiar: I'll open a temporary test quota for Sentinel so the replay can start as soon as traces arrive.
[06:31] Rajiv Patel: We'll send the 48-hour sample by Thursday.
[06:34] Jordan Li: Great — thanks everyone, call adjourned.
